oneLiner: A 27%-growth ad franchise that re-rated ~27% in September 2026 on the Muse personal-agent launch, now asking investors to underwrite $130-145B of capex, near-zero FCF and a ~$10B Q3 legal charge.
thesis: Ad machine still accelerating. Q2 2026 ad revenue rose 27% YoY to $59.4B with impressions +14% and price per ad +12% - AI is lifting volume and pricing simultaneously.

AI monetization beyond ads is now a product. Muse, a personal AI agent on Muse Spark models, launched Sept 8, 2026 (US/Canada; free tier plus reported $20/$100 monthly plans) and reached ~5M downloads in 22 days per Sensor Tower.

Unmatched distribution. 3.60B daily active people (Q2 2026) give Muse and Meta AI instant scale via WhatsApp and the apps; FoA other revenue crossed $1B/quarter (+73% YoY) on paid messaging and subscriptions.

Hardware as an agent endpoint. Connect (Sept 23, 2026) launched Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 ($449), camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio ($349), $1,300 Meta VR Glasses for spring 2027, and plans to bring Muse to glasses.
Street turned. JPMorgan (Overweight since its Sept 2026 upgrade) lifted its target to $920 from $820 on Sept 24; average target ~$794 (late Sept 2026, Yahoo via Admirals).

latestProse: Q2 2026 revenue was $60.8B, +28% YoY, with ads at $59.4B (+27%) on impressions +14% and pricing +12%. Operating margin compressed to 31% from 43% as expenses jumped 55% to $42.0B - including $2.4B of unspecified legal accruals and $1.18B severance from ~8,000 AI-pivot layoffs - and EPS fell 13% to $6.18, the first miss in seven quarters. Reality Labs lost $4.62B on $431M revenue; FoA earned $23.4B. The disclosure that matters most: capex of $31.1B drove free cash flow down ~91% to $784M - the AI buildout is consuming nearly all cash generation.
guidanceProse: Q3 2026 revenue is guided to $61-64B (July 29, unchanged). 2026 capex guidance is $130-145B (narrowed from $125-145B) and 2026 operating income is guided above 2025's $83.3B - but Meta has since flagged a ~$10B Q3 legal charge from the August youth settlement. No 2027 capex guide yet; third-party estimates run ~$186B (consensus) to $210-215B (Deutsche Bank). The debate: bulls say Muse and AI ad returns fund the buildout; bears see FCF near zero, rising debt and a 2027 depreciation wave.

guide.label: 2026 capex guide
guide.sub: unchanged since July; Q2 FCF $784M; ~$10B Q3 legal charge flagged

segments: Family of Apps: $60.4B revenue (99.3% of total), $23.4B operating income; other revenue >$1B (+73%) on WhatsApp paid messaging/subscriptions
Reality Labs: $431M (~0.7%), -$4.62B operating loss; pivoting from Quest VR toward AI glasses
competitive: Digital ads: duopoly with Google; Amazon scaling retail media; TikTok remains the engagement rival for Reels (current share splits unverified)
AI agents: Muse vs OpenAI's Dots (launched Sept 29, 2026, paid tiers only) and Gemini agents; Amazon blocked Muse from its shopping site on Sept 20, 2026
Open models: shift from open Llama to a hybrid/closed Muse Spark strategy cedes some open-weights leadership
Wearables: Ray-Ban Meta leads consumer AI glasses; Meta VR Glasses ($1,300, spring 2027) take on Apple Vision Pro
moat: 3.6B daily users and the deepest commercial-intent dataset outside Google feed self-reinforcing ad-targeting models rivals cannot replicate at scale. Advantage+'s $75B run-rate shows the AI flywheel converting into pricing power, and ~$60B/quarter of revenue funds a compute arms race few can match.
risks: Capex crushes free cash flow. H1 2026 capex was $50.9B, so the $130-145B guide implies ~$40-47B/quarter in H2; Q2 FCF was $784M and long-term debt rose to $83.7B (June 30, 2026) from $58.7B at end-2025.

Legal bill crystallizing. Up to $18B youth settlement over 10 years (approved Aug 26, 2026); New Mexico privacy verdict (Sept 25) with the state seeking $35-40B vs Meta's proposed $3.45B cap; FTC appeal; school-district trials from Feb 3, 2027.
Teen time limits. The settlement imposes a default two-hour daily cap for 13-17s on Facebook/Instagram, a potential drag on US impressions (size unverified).
Muse execution. Retention unpublished, privacy/security flaws reported, OpenAI Dots launched Sept 29, and MSL attrition continues (Andrew Tulloch left Sept 2026).
Concentration and rates: ~98% of revenue is advertising; the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sept 16, 2026.
catalysts: Oct 2026: New Mexico judge sets privacy penalty (state seeks $35-40B)
Oct 13, 2026: Ray-Ban Meta Audio ships; Display glasses launch in Germany/France/Italy
Oct 28, 2026 (expected, unconfirmed by Meta): Q3 2026 earnings - ~$10B legal charge, first Muse metrics, early 2027 capex view
~Late Jan 2027: Q4 2026 results and full 2027 guidance (estimated); Feb 3, 2027: school-district MDL trials begin
Spring 2027: Meta VR Glasses launch; ongoing FTC appeal at the D.C. Circuit and EU DMA/DSA proceedings
pricedIn: At $725.93 (Oct 1, 2026 close), META trades ~27x trailing GAAP and ~22.9x 2026 / ~21x 2027 consensus EPS ($31.72 / ~$34.90) - back near its ~26.5x 5-year average P/E after a ~27% September rally that peaked at $779.82 on Sept 24. Average analyst target is ~$794 (88% Buy). The price now credits Muse with real option value; with FCF yield ~2% and Q3 EPS revisions skewed down (5 up / 35 down over 90 days), Q3 must show Muse traction and a tolerable 2027 capex number.

scenarios.bear: Muse usage fades against OpenAI Dots, 2027 capex lands above ~$215B, and New Mexico plus other legal outcomes add >$10B in charges on top of the settlement. FCF stays near zero, the multiple compresses toward ~17-18x 2027 EPS: stock $580-620.
scenarios.base: Ads keep compounding ~20%+, Q3 lands in the $61-64B range, 2027 capex $190-210B, and Muse shows early paid conversion. Multiple holds ~21-22x 2027 EPS: $720-780.
scenarios.bull: Muse discloses strong retention and subscription/transaction revenue, glasses become its endpoint, and ads grow >25% while capex peaks as a share of revenue. META re-rates as an AI platform at 25x+, toward JPMorgan's $920 target.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: TTM FCF is crushed by the $130-145B capex program (Q2 2026 FCF $784M; FCF yield ~2%), so an FCF-DCF would misread the investment cycle as value destruction.
